After a couple of decent thrusts down the left, England’s right flank gets weaving with Rogers finding the overlapping James whose cross is smothered by Argentina.

The referee Ismail Elfath is really being tested in these early stages. Chiefly by Argentina. Paredes is after Bellingham. Every challenge on Messi is claimed as a foul by Argentina.

It’s clear this is going to be a huge test of the England players’ ability to concentrate on their plan, and to not get drawn into the emotion of the game. On top of that, Argentina are a good side and they are probing for weaknesses. They have come out very aggressively.

England have started well. They look confident and dangerous – more than Argentina. Argentina want to make this a dark arts game. They are better than us at that ‘nasty’ stuff. We can’t get involved in any of that.

Wonderful tackle by Paredes on Bellingham instigates an Argentina counter during which Messi claims he was fouled. He wasn’t but that doesn’t stop him waving his arms around in exasperation. England try to attack up the left only to be stopped by a foul on Gordon. From the quickly taken free-kick, Spence makes great headway down the left, beating Molina again only for Fernandez to race back and force him off the ball and into touch.

Somebody is going to boil over here. Paredes and Fernandez are constantly looking to goad England’s players, much to the chagrin of Thomas Tuchel and captain Harry Kane, who seems to be urging US referee Ismail Elfath to take closer control.

Excellent combination between Gordon and Spence down the England left gets the better of Molina. He cuts in, takes a touch too many which takes him into five Argentina defenders who swarm round him with recovery runs. Sheer weight of numbers push him back.

A foul on Rogers ends with a drop ball after Anderson was deemed to have hurt Paredes in a firm but not illegal tackle. The ref is going to have to get a card out soon. Tuchel is going garrity with Scaloni and the level of diving by Argentina. The most naked example of that is when Simeone picks up the ball having been caught offside and Pickford bumps him as he tries to get it back. Simeone goes down as if kneecapped.

Gordon chases a long pass down the left that has too much on it but he gets there in the nick of time but can’t find Rogers’ run down the inside-left channel. Emi Martinez gathers.

Anderson buys a third free-kick off Simeone with excellent positioning but, after Kane is tackled by Paredes, he fouls Fernandez in this tit for tat start.

Rogers drives at Tagliafico, reaches the byline and whips over a cross that Argentina head behind for a corner. Rice goes long. Simeone wrestles Stones over but the referee waves play on until a high boot clips Messi.

Spence makes good progress down the left, riding a tackle before a forceful sliding tackle wins the ball back. England regroup and Simeone fouls Anderson .

Bellingham and Paredes were mouthing off at each other after that Fernandez foul on Anderson. Messi then had a go at Bellingham too. Feisty start!

England continue to press high and there’s a stand-off between the players with the gobby Paredes in Bellingham’s face after Messi is not given a free-kick when Anderson holds his shoulder. Fernandez retaliates with a chop down Anderson’s shin. Messi, trying to referee the game, gets up in the referee’s grill.

Argentine fans drown out the God Save The King with their own song. England fans respond in kind with the Argentinian anthem. This is a real World Cup knockout tie - and nothing even the stadium address system can do about it. It’s electric in the stadium. I was in Dallas yesterday for the first semi-final and the mood was nothing like as fierce as this.

Argentina kick off, attacking from right to left. Messi, alone in the centre-circle, rolls it to Paredes who works it all the way back to Emi Martinez. England press high and force a throw-in.

England give the ball to the centre-backs who sweep it across the back four. Mac Allister tries to disrupt the spell of possession with a shove.

Michael Buffer’s “champions of the worrrrrrld” billing for England feels a touch generous given it was 60 years ago. I have watched him perform his master of ceremonies shtick in several sports and he barely changes a word. Still, it has earned him, at a conservative estimate, £300m.

God Save the King goes first and is resoundingly booed by the Argentina fans. England supporters respond by whistling and jeering through Himno Nacional Argentino.

England fans are certainly outnumbered inside the Atlanta stadium, with pockets of Argentina fans in among the main England sections. It has all seem good-natured so far, so let’s hope that lasts.

Pleased to report that Sir Mick Jagger is here and singing along to ‘Sweet Caroline’. TV cameras have located him.

Reporters from all countries sitting together. I’m assuming my neighbour is Argentine judging by the maté and Lionel Messi flask.

Governor of the Falkland Islands, Colin Martin-Reynolds lights up Government House with the colours of the England flag.

It’s just a feeling, a stomach feeling from the coach about Morgan. He has something special tp give today. He was very good in the last game against Norway and had an outstanding training session to follow up on that performance.

We need to play with freedom, also for the mindset, we should be ready for the fight, calm and collected to give them some problems to solve. We’re up for it.

Lionel Scaloni has given a nod to the historic rivalry of this fixture by picking Diego Simeone’s son in his starting line-up. Giuliano Simeone is given his first appearance since the final group stage match against Jordan, when Argentina had already sealed a place in the knockouts. His father was famously on the end of David Beckham’s boot 28 years ago in Saint-Étienne. This just adds to the feeling there will be some flashpoint in the next few hours in Atlanta.

While Thomas Tuchel has changed his backline, Argentina are playing the same back four from the team that defeated Switzerland. Simeone is the only change, coming in for Rodrigo De Paul. This could mean a change of system for the world champions – if Enzo Fernández drifts to the right, they could look very 4-4-2.

It doesn’t get much bigger, the biggest competition in football against the holders.

We know what Argentina are about. We’ve got a game plan we’re ready to set up against.

The manager’s made a decision. Morgan is an incredible player, he’s fast, strong and can come inside. He’s a player we’re all looking forward to playing with.

I’m back to normal. I’m 100 per cent, fully refreshed and ready to go.

The team will shock a few people because of Djed Spence’s inclusion. What I like about Thomas Tuchel’s approach is that keeping the same team would be a much easier decision, particularly in a game of this magnitude.

The manager is consistent in selecting players for specialist roles. Just as he called up Dan Burn in case England needed to revert to a back five (as they did against Mexico), the reason he likes Spence is for situations requiring one-on-one defending. Tuchel clearly believes Spence’s pace is a vital attribute in this situation, even if facing Lionel Messi is the ultimate challenge. This is the whole point of Spence being in the squad. If England win, the same logic would suggest he would be asked to mark Lamine Yamal in the final.

From that perspective, maybe we should not be so shocked by the choice.

Morgan Rogers comes in because Tuchel simply could not go with Madueke again. He was poor against Norway, and Saka has not looked fully fit all tournament. Saka is still a good option from the bench.

Overall, Rogers has played well whenever he’s been given a chance, so he’s gone with the man showing form.

This is the first game where England are playing a team who will expect to have as much of, if not more, of the ball than us. Every other game has followed the same pattern, certainly at the start, where England were considered the higher level team and tried to go after the opponent.

That’s not necessarily going to be the case here because we are clearly not favourites, and Argentina will look to apply all the early pressure. Argentina have the edge coming into the match because they are a team that has shown in recent international tournaments that they know how to get over the line.

England deserve to be at this stage, but the question remains: do we have the capacity to do what is habitual for nations like Argentina – finding a way when it matters most in the latter stages of a World Cup?

This is a night for bravery, which means getting on the ball and controlling the game. That could be achieved against every other opponent in this tournament so far, even if some of the victories have been flawed. Doing so against Argentina requires another layer of courage.

Britain’s ambassador to the United States has urged England fans to remain on their best behaviour as tensions mount ahead of the World Cup semi-final against Argentina.

Sir Christian Turner called on travelling supporters in Atlanta to continue to act as “ambassadors for the country” amid fears that the historic dispute over the Falkland Islands could spill into violence.

The FBI has designated Wednesday night’s match “high risk”, making it the most serious security concern of the tournament so far.

“Continue to support each other, whatever the outcome,” Sir Chris told The Telegraph. “Enjoy the moment, enjoy the occasion, enjoy the hospitality. It’s a game of football.”

Tensions have been inflamed by recent claims from the Argentine government that Britain is an “usurping” power and that the Falkland Islanders were “artificially implanted”.

So far, England’s games in the tournament have seen little to no violence.

Of the estimated 50,000 fans who have made the journey to the United States for the World Cup, just 25 needed assistance from the embassy for issues like lost passports, medical problems, or visa help.

“It’s a wonderful sign of how the fans have been ambassadors for the country,” Sir Chris added.

Ian Wright has attracted criticism from Falklands veterans after predicting England’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina will be a “war”.

The former Arsenal and England striker was previewing tonight’s tie as part of ITV’s coverage of Spain’s victory over France on Tuesday evening.

“There’s going to be chaos in the game; there’s going to be chaos in the stands; they’re not separating the fans. It’s a game where we’re going to have to show a lot of composure,” said Wright, who won 33 caps for England.

“It’s a country that, as time’s gone by, I’ve learnt a lot about them, and I have no love for them. Obviously, [Diego] Maradona’s somebody that’s done some amazing things I’ve seen.

“It’s a team that we have to beat and it’s going to be a tough one; it’s going to be a real tough one, a real attritional war we’re going into, and we have to recognise that.

“I’ve heard Thomas Tuchel saying it’s just a game. It’s not just a game, and they’ll realise it’s not just a game. It’s going to be more than that when they play.”

255 British soldiers lost their lives during the 1982 Falklands War. Simon Weston, who suffered severe burns during the Argentine bombing of the Galahad Ship, condemned the comparison between a football match and war.

“Some people describe a footballer as a hero on the field but that’s completely misusing the language,” he told The Telegraph. “They’re footballers. It’s hardly like they’re risking their lives on the pitch. It’s nothing like a battlefield.”

Marc Guéhi has claimed there is “no pressure at all” on England ahead of their semi-final against Argentina.

The England centre-back said the onus was on Argentina to win the game as World Cup holders.

“What’s the pressure? The onus is on them, they are the world champions,” Guéhi said.

“They need to come out and defend their title so there is no pressure on us at all.”

We’re still around five hours from any official announcement on team news, but the early indications are that Thomas Tuchel is considering retaining the back line that started England’s extra-time victory over Norway.

Tuchel deployed a back four containing Ezri Konsa, John Stones, Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly in the previous round before introducing Reece James, Djed Spence and Dan Burn off the bench.

James, the Chelsea right-back, is available to start from the off in Atlanta after recovering from a hamstring injury he picked up in the goalless draw with Ghana.

Tuchel opted to field Konsa at right-back in the absence of James and the suspended Jarell Quansah and could stick with the Aston Villa defender after impressing against Erling Haaland and Co.

Elsewhere, Declan Rice is likely to keep his starting place in midfield. The Arsenal midfielder was withdrawn at half-time against Norway after being struck down with a stomach bug in the build-up to the game but has sufficiently recovered to be considered for selection this evening.

The other dilemma facing Tuchel is who to start on the right side of attack. Bukayo Saka impressed after replacing Noni Madueke against Norway, but there have been previous concerns over a chronic Achilles issue.

Tuchel also has the option of bringing in Marcus Rashford and playing him on the right or switching Anthony Gordon from the left. Morgan Rogers, the Aston Villa playmaker is another option on the right side of attack after he made an impressive contribution off the bench in the quarter-finals.

For those requiring a detailed history on the acrimony at the heart of this storied rivalry, look no further than Sam Wallace’s excellent essay, which explains why this tie will always be more than just a football match.

Here’s a snippet of Sam on the fixture’s most infamous chapter: the 1986 World Cup quarter-final, which took place four years after the Falklands War.

“You can’t grasp what it all means to the people back home, but something tells you it is the greatest experience you will have as a player.” Gary Lineker, with a hat-trick against Poland and two more goals in the last-16 win over Paraguay, had assessed the mood correctly before England’s match against Argentina at the Estadio Azteca. But even he could not have guessed what was to come.

The war between Britain and Argentina, just four years earlier, hung heavily over the game. “I am a football manager, not a politician,” Bobby Robson, the England manager, said: “Don’t ask me that sort of question.”

Midfielder Glenn Hoddle warned that Maradona had learned from his experiences at the 1982 World Cup and “really come on strong”. He pondered whether England should man-mark Maradona and suggested left-back Kenny Sansom. “I don’t think we should change the way we play because of him,” Hoddle said. “You would have to re-shape the whole side.”

The Argentine players gave each of the England team a present before the game. Maradona punched the ball into the England goal in the 51st minute. His brilliant second was four minutes later. Lineker scored his sixth of the tournament and England lost 2-1.

In just over 10 hours time we will know the identity of Spain’s World Cup final opponents after the European champions dispatched 2018 winners and pre-tournament favourites France on Tuesday evening.

Immortality beckons for England, who are braced for their biggest match in a generation with familiar foes Argentina standing between them and a first World Cup final since 1966.

This is a fixture steeped in history. The two nations are meeting at a World Cup for the sixth time, renewing a bitter rivalry that has produced some of the tournament’s most memorable moments and enduring controversies.

Thomas Tuchel’s side have reached the last four without being entirely convincing. They needed extra time to beat Norway in the quarter-finals after surviving for over half an hour with 10 men against co-hosts Mexico in the previous round.

England’s fortunes have been intrinsically linked to the performances of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham, who have scored six goals apiece to keep Tuchel’s side alive at this tournament.

Argentina’s route to the latter stages has been just as arduous. The defending champions needed extra time to overcome both Cape Verde and Switzerland, while they came from 2-0 down with 11 minutes remaining to beat Egypt and avoid one of the biggest shocks in World Cup history.

The holders remain on course to become only the third side after Italy (1934, 1938) and Brazil (1958, 1962) to retain their crown and in the process give Lionel Messi the fairy-tale end to a remarkable international career.

The 39-year-old has scored eight goals in the tournament and remains central to everything to Argentina’s fortunes. Remarkably, despite a career spanning more than two decades, tonight’s semi-final meeting will be Messi’s first ever international appearance against England.

Tuchel has spoken openly about the scale of the challenge facing his players. Stopping Messi has become one of football’s great unsolved problems, but the 52-year-old German insists his team must focus on imposing their own game plan rather than being consumed with the

Rarely has so much been at stake for both nations. For England, it is another chance to move one step closer to ending a wait that has now stretched almost 60 years. For Argentina, it is an opportunity to go level with Italy and Germany for the second-most World Cup titles (four). Either way, one of football’s most storied rivalries is about to add another chapter.

#2269. ‘Surely’: Reporter makes bold prediction regarding ‘outstanding’ Middlesbrough summer recruit

Middlesbrough signed the attacker from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer and he penned a long-term five-year deal at the Riverside Stadium running until June 2031. He has since adapted well to life at Boro and has been prolific for Kim Hellberg‘s side.

Lankshear, 21, has made 16 appearances in all competitions this season, 13 of which have come in the Championship. He has chipped in with an eye-catching 15 goals already.

Journalist Cottier has delivered his verdict, as per a report by BBC Sport: “Fifteen goals in all competitions is an outstanding number to have reached before the end of October and Middlesbrough look to have quelled any concerns that they cannot be in this promotion race for the long haul. They are exciting, creative and solid at the back – and in Lankshear they have a young Englishman surely destined to get senior international recognition in the not-too-distant future.”

Middlesbrough beat Charlton Athletic 3-0 at home last time out and remain top of the table above Swansea City, Wolves and West Brom after 13 fixtures. They are back in action on Wednesday away at Wrexham as they aim to keep their momentum going for as long as possible.

Middlesbrough’s decision to snap up Lankshear from Tottenham Hotspur has turned out to be a masterstroke. He has established himself as Boro’s most prized asset.

Boro lacked a proper number nine in the last campaign and that was mainly the reason why they missed out on the top two. They then lacked a cutting edge in the play-offs, hence why they eventually lost to Hull City in the final at Wembley in May.

Lankshear has answered their prayers though and he has more than proved that he knows where the back of the net is. He is already on 15 goals and November has only just begun.

The ex-Arsenal and Sheffield United man played six times during his days at Tottenham Hotspur before they sold him permanently. He also had loan spells away from Spurs at West Brom and Oxford United to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

Middlesbrough ace Lankshear is one of the most exciting young English players around at the moment. The fact he is playing every week at Boro and not sitting around on Tottenham Hotspur’s bench will be doing him the world of good.

Hellberg’s men are on a roll right now but they can’t afford to be complacent as they aim to claw themselves into the top flight this term. They will need to be at their best to get another three points against Wrexham later this week.

“Libera la Lazio” è quello che si legge dal cartello mostrato da Gioacchino

La storia che ha commosso tutti è quella di Giocchino e Luigi, due partecipanti della maratona di New York. Come riportato da La Repubblica, sono due cugini originari di Favara. Luigi Sorce, 22 anni, è in carrozzina per una paralisi celebrale dalla nascita ed è stato il cugino, Gioacchino Alaimo, a spingerlo per tutti i 42 chilometri nella categoria Duo Team.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

I ragazzi sono due tifosi biancocelesti, dai commoventi filmati viene ripreso un cartello mostrato da Gioacchino con scritto: “Libera la Lazio”. Una maratona con la Lazio nel cuore, un popolo unito da un grande amore per i colori biancocelesti.

Gioacchino e Luigi sono due nostri giovani straordinari. Favara stanotte era rappresentata oltreoceano, sulle strade della maratona di New York, con un messaggio straordinario di amore, coraggio e inclusione.

#2267. Mandas vittoria di Gattuso: pagato neanche 1 mln, la Juve voleva scambiarlo con Di Gregorio

Christos Mandas è una delle sorprese più interessanti della Serie A, ormai non ci sono più dubbi. Il portiere greco della Lazio, classe 2001, è il secondo per clean sheet dopo Guglielmo Vicario: quattro porte inviolate contro cinque, ossia il 40,0% delle partite giocate. Un rendimento che assume ancora più valore se si guarda al costo dell'operazione: Lotito lo ha acquistato infatti dall'OFI Creta nel settembre 2023 per appena 951.000 euro, lasciandolo in prestito in Grecia per un'altra stagione. Ma quanto vale oggi Christos Mandas? Almeno 20-25 milioni di euro, complice il contratto fino al 2029.

Eppure, la scorsa estate, Mandas avrebbe potuto prendere un'altra strada. La Juventus aveva seriamente messo gli occhi sul greco, valutando anche un possibile incastro di mercato con Michele Di Gregorio.. Sul numero 35, appena rientrato dal prestito poco fruttuoso al Bournemouth (zero presenze), c'erano i bianconeri e c'era pure la Fiorentina. Alla fine, però, mister Gennaro Gattuso ha fatto muro, convincendo il giocatore a restare a Roma e puntando su di lui come estremo difensore titolare. "Il mister mi ha dato fiducia dall'inizio della stagione, io ho bisogno di questo. Mi fa allenare tanto, mi aiuta tanto nel gioco di piede e voglio fare di tutto per lui e per la squadra", ha dichiarato Mandas dopo il 2-1 col Cagliari.

I numeri stanno decisamente dando ragione all'allenatore dei capitolini: 11 presenze, 10 gol subiti e, appunto, ben quattro clean sheet. A questi si aggiungono il rigore neutralizzato a Yeboah contro il Venezia, sullo 0-0, e tante parate decisive nell'economia dei nove successi della sua Lazio. Detto altrimenti: Mandas non è più soltanto una promessa da valorizzare, ma una delle certezze della squadra prima in classifica. E anche un investimento economico che, grazie a Gattuso, è fruttato molto più del previsto...

#2266. Meret in conferenza stampa: “I dettagli fanno la differenza. La stagione non sta andando come volevamo”

Alex Meret, portiere del Napoli, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo la sconfitta contro la Juventus: “I dettagli sbagliati? Fanno la differenza, probabilmente dovevamo essere più attenti e cattivi nell’evitare di far calciare i loro attaccanti con due grandissimi gol. E’ un peccato, è stata una partita equilibrata che volevamo vincere come loro, i dettagli hanno fatto la differenza come la qualità dei loro attaccanti che è stata fondamentale per farci perdere la partita. La stagione non sta andando come volevamo, c’è il tempo, la qualità e la voglia di tutti per riprenderci, ci sono tanti alti e bassi e non possiamo permettercelo. Però vogliamo recuperare il terreno in classifica, serve lavorare con fiducia e ottimismo e consapevolezza delle nostre qualità. Ci stanno mancando i dettagli, ma sappiamo che possiamo riprenderci e risalire la classifica. Cambio mentale tra primo e secondo tempo? Non credo sia stato un grande primo tempo, ma equilibrato, abbiamo cercato di fare gol. Il secondo tempo non abbiamo creato tanto davanti, ci sono state poche occasioni e dovevamo sfruttarle meglio. La partita è stata decisa da un gran tiro, dopo l’espulsione sono venute meno le distanze perchè volevamo pareggiarla. Serve essere fiduciosi”.

#2263. Four chances created: 30-year-old justifies new Southampton contract talk with starring role in QPR thrashing

Southampton continued their rise up the Championship table on Saturday as they defeated QPR 4-1, making it five undefeated. The Saints are now up in 5th, recovering well from the four-point deduction they started the campaign with.

It was a fine display from Tonda Eckert’s side in their routine triumph. The goals were shared across the team with Kuryu Matsuki, Cam Bragg, Keven Schlotterbeck and Welington netting, but one man who had a key role in two of the goals was Ryan Manning.

It was Manning’s pull-back that Bragg converted from for the second, and a deep corner of his found Schlotterbeck completely free at the back post to make it 3-0. In a week where news has emerged of Southampton’s talks to renew his contract, the 30-year-old further strengthened the case for his deal.

Creation was where Manning stood out on Saturday. Alongside his aforementioned pair of assists, the Irishman created the joint-most chances in the game with four – tied with Southampton teammate Finn Azaz.

His set-piece ability was on display as a deep, in-swinging cross to the back stick almost saw centre-back Schlotterbeck score in the first half too. Manning took five corners and delivered two successful crosses from open play.

Manning didn’t have much defending to do as he made only three defensive contributions against his former side QPR. However, he was victorious in four of his six ground duels and made three recoveries as well (all stats via Fotmob).

The Saints star’s contributions now put him on one goal and three assists in 13 Championship games this term. He set up one goal in the 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Colchester United at the start of the season too.

Southampton fans won’t have had many complaints when news of Manning’s new contract talks emerged. He has grown into an influential player under Eckert with his creative abilities from left-back making him a valuable asset.

His case for a new deal has only grown stronger with his performance from QPR though. The technical ability he offers makes the Saints such a threat from wide areas and set plays.

A new contract would be a justified reward for how Manning has grown at St. Mary’s. Like many, he struggled during their last stay in the Premier League in 2024/25, but he will be determined to earn another shot as Southampton battle for promotion from the Championship this season.

#2262. Spalletti in conferenza stampa: “Successo meritato, complimenti ai ragazzi”

Luciano Spalletti, allenatore della Juventus, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo la vittoria contro il Napoli: “I calciatori hanno messo mano a questa voglia di riguadagnarsi la fiducia dei nostri tifosi, hanno fatto duelli e corse per i compagni e per la squadra, senza avere il dubbio di buttare via una corsa e hanno vinto una partita in maniera meritata. Gli si fanno i complimenti, se questo primo passo non lo fanno da soli quando si cade in basso, diventa difficile dire e fare qualsiasi cosa. Solo loro possono fare certe cose, se non fai duelli e vinci i contrasti e hai il coraggio di avere campo libero alle spalle per dargli addosso e guadagnare metri, di rimanere alti con tre attaccanti come nel secondo tempo. Tu stai lì, li aiuti affinchè arrivi uno che fa il primo passo che è contagioso per tutti gli altri, si torna ad avere una mezza identità e si vince una partita fondamentale con enormi difficoltà. Fino ad ora perdevo, io però ora posso dire che siamo in tredici, non ho i cambi. Altrimenti dico come tutti, datemi le armi per essere a livello. Oggi non possiamo essere paragonati a nessuno, oggi tutti a urlare su Cambiaso ma chi potevo far entrare? Non ce ne sono altri, mi piaceva far giocare altri ma a qualcuno puoi dedicare la partita del giovedì. Vediamo come sta Cabal e come sta McKennie, poi se alle scuderie fa comodo dire che la Juventus deve vincere lo scudetto e fa comodo portare avanti certe idee. Se gli si leva pressione giocano con più tranquillità, oggi non si può competere per niente e se non recuperiamo qualcuno si rimane in questa situazione. Per noi era una partita enormemente difficile, il Napoli aveva gli stessi punti nostri e mi sembra di esser arrivato diversamente al match: loro hanno vinto a Monza e noi abbiamo perso. Abbiamo fatto leva sulle debolezze del Napoli e viceversa? Il Napoli ha preso in mano la gara e ci ha creato difficoltà nell’agganciarli, non riuscivamo a trovare quello che era il nostro avversario nelle scalate e negli scivolamenti di squadra. Ci sono venuti addosso uomo contro uomo, noi tentando di aiutare e mettere in condizione l’attaccante non ci riuscivamo nel primo tempo. Vicario ha fatto una gran parata su Lucca, poi abbiamo fatto qualche duello a viso aperto e siamo migliorati, è stata una partita sottolivello per entrambe al 45′. Poi siamo rimasti su con i tre attaccanti nella ripresa, Di Lorenzo non c’era più e nel ruolo è il migliore a spingere. Qualche volta ci abbiamo provato in maniera sconquassata, il nostro stadio col suo supporto è la vera faccia di chi partecipa al fianco della squadra. C’è voluto un gran gol di Alajbegovic, lui ha questo tiro da fuori, e poi Boga come gli altri nella ripresa sono entrati bene, con la fiducia di chi aveva già messo mano alla situazione. Il Napoli? Lo sa meglio Allegri, l’ho abbracciato a fine partita: ci siamo incontrati e salutati, è un piacere come sempre perchè non è vero che con lui non parlo perchè ci siamo antipatici. Ci siamo fatti i viaggi in treno assieme, Landucci è stato due giorni interi a casa mia in campagna, poi voi volete scrivere che Landucci mi ha detto delle brutte cose, dipende dalla scuderia alla quale appartenete. Cabal ha giocato una partita straordinaria, anche in un ruolo non suo andando ad attaccare, secondo me è stato uno dei migliori. Il modulo? Quando giochi contro difese così, anche se giochi a cinque contro tre attaccanti la difesa la devi rompere e noi abbiamo deciso di farlo con McKennie e Kalulu su Olivera e Lang. Se loro hanno un solo attaccante non puoi rimanere a cinque, devi cambiare la sua organizzazione e fisionomia di sistema di gioco. Però la mia era una idea voluta, nel secondo tempo sarebbe stato più basso McKennie perchè Alajbegovic volevo tenerlo più alto senza Di Lorenzo”.

#2261. Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Sam Smith with the winning moment 🤌🔴⚪️#WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/YzTvnzIpz6

Twenty-one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side entirely composed of academy products, facing a decent test against a Wrexham side now including the likes of Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

We knew it wouldn’t be perfect - that’s only natural for the first pre-season game - and the main thing is that everybody came through it in good shape. No injuries so we can move onto the next step next week.

[Andrey Santos] and Mason [Mount] did some really good things and connected really well. There’s loads of little positives to take. The sharpness at the top end will come as we move through pre-season.

I was really pleased with the second half team. They controlled the game really well against a team who aren’t easy to play against. The boys took responsibility and their quality; they can really be proud of themselves.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. The senior players looked understandably rusty, and a very youthful replacement XI were more dominant than their seniors. But they struggled to create clear chances and Wrexham deserved their win.

Full-time in Helsinki 🇫🇮First pre-season minutes in the tank for 22 Reds ✔️

Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

Man Utd’s youngsters continue to press for an equaliser. They haven’t created much but the rest of their second-half performance has been impressive.

Ward makes another comfortable save, this time when Shea Lacey tries his luck from 22 yards.

The left-back Harry Amass beats his man and curls a cross that bounces towards Ethan Wheatley at the near post. He stabs it goalwards and Ward makes a comfortable save. Tough chance, though Wheatley did well to get across the defender.

Man Utd’s best move of the second half. Dan Gore runs onto a return pass from Shea Lacey and sweeps a low ball into the six-yard box that is held at the second attempt by Danny Ward.

Wrexham substitution Alex Moore replaces Aaron James, who was the only starter on either side to play part of the second half.

The first chance of the second half falls to Wrexham. After a neat move through midfield, Davis Keillor-Dunn gallops into the area and drives a low shot that Radek Vitek saves well with his legs.

Kamason is booked for a late tackle on Dobson. That looked a bit harsh, certainly in a friendly.

Wrexham - in a back five, heaven forfend - are defending well and keeping the opposition at arm’s length. Unlike Argentina, Man Utd haven’t really tried any crosses yet.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

And this is the youthful XI that Michael Carrick has put out for the second half.

Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Vitek; Kamason, Devaney, Armer, Amass; Collyer, T Fletcher; Lacey, Gore, Williams; Wheatley.

Wrexham have made 10 changes, with Aaron James the only survivor from the first half. This is their new XI.

Our second-half XI 👇🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/pechlNMwxJ

Manchester United begin the second half having made 11 changes at half-time. We’ll have the full teams shortly, all being well.

Wrexham lead after a low-key first half in Helsinki. Sam Smith scored to enliven a half of few chances. Andrey Santos was lively on his Manchester United debut, gobbling up the ground defensively and playing forward at every opportunity.

We should have very different teams - perhaps completely new XIs - for the second half.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

Man Utd hit the bar Mason Mount’s inswinging corner from the left is headed against his own crossbar by Sam Smith, woh was off balance as he challenged Leny Yoro. That’s the closest we’ve come to a goal at either end.

Broadhead wriggles away from Andrey Santos on the edge of the area, but Santos snaps back at him and Broadhead curls over the bar.

Zirkzee pulls up gingerly after being caught by a Wrexham player. Looks like an in impact injury rather than a muscle problem.

Santos and Mount probe on the edge of the Wrexham area. A through ball is cut out and rebounds towards Zirkzee, who whistles a snapshot wide from 20 yards. Not a bad effort.

Patrick Dorgu’s shot is blocked on the edge of the area. United are starting to find a bit of rhythm after a slow start.

Cadamarteri surges into the area and is about to shoot when Heaven makes an excellent lunging challenge. Wrexham look more likely to score at this point.

Smith barges Andrey Santos over long after the ball has gone. A bit of a needless challenge, one that Santos did not especially appreciate.

Both teams look rusty, United in particular. Wrexham have been a bit more direct and slightly more dangerous in attack.

Andrey Santos loses the ball in midfield, leading to a one-on-one chance for Sam Smith that is well saved by Heaten. Smith was offside so it wouldn’t have counted.

That opportunity aside, it’s been a predictably quiet start - lots of passing in midfield from United in particular.

The new signing Andrey Santos makes an important interception after 40 seconds. Nathan Broadhead seemed to foul the keeper Tom Heaton in the United area, but play continued and Broadhead’s ball across was turned behind by Santos.

Wrexham, in their blue change strip, kick off from right to left as we watch.

Both teams line up for the usual pre-match formalities. Harry Maguire and Matty James, a former Man Utd academy player, are the captains.

We’ve been back in training 10 days and we’re taking it step by step. It’s great to be back at it again.

Andrey Santos is a fantastic character and he’s settled in really well. He’s buzzing to be here and he’ll do really well for us. We’re not expecting anything crazy special today - it’s a step, just get your eye in and get back on the pitch. I’m really looking forward to the progression he shows while he’s here.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford after United triggered his release clause at Aston Villa.

The Belgium international played a key role in helping Villa lift the Europa League last season, but pushed for the move to United after turning down the offer of a new contract in the West Midlands.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

“Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.”

I’m not sure when Man Utd last played Wrexham in a friendly, but the most recent competitive meeting between the sides was in January 1995. It was three days after Eric Cantona tried to kick xenophobia out of football at Selhurst Park, so United’s 5-2 win was somewhat overshadowed.

Andrey Santos starts in what is a pretty strong United XI.

Lining up for our first fixture of pre-season! 🇫🇮Watch LIVE on MUTV ⤵️

Our first-half XI in Helsinki 🇫🇮🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/WrXbc2B7JQ

The World Cup final? Pah! The 2026-27 Premier League season is just over a month away, and Manchester United’s pre-season begins this afternoon with a friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki.

Man Utd have started many seasons with a whimper since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, but there’s plenty of summer optimism around Old Trafford. Michael Carrick overachieved so spectacularly as caretaker manager that a full-time appointment became inevitable. Now all he has to do is maintain that league form across a full season while also juggling the Champions League.

United have filled part of their midfield void by signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans is having a post-World Cup break but Santos is part of a United squad that also includes Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro.

“Everything about Manchester United is special,” said Santos after signing for the club earlier in the week. “It is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented. As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick. He is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.”

Wrexham have ambitions to play United in a competitive fixture sooner rather than later. They missed out on the Championship playoffs but will go again with a very similar squad.

“This is a great test for us, it really is,” said their manager Phil Parkinson. “As always, when we were in the other divisions we looked to these games as a test and this will be absolutely no different.

“The out-of-possession stuff becomes really important against the better quality teams. But as we’ve always done, we’re not just going to these games to stop the opposition.”

After 55 long days...It's a United matchday! 🇾🇪❤️

#2260. Gollini torna a Old Trafford. Ricordate quando è stato un giocatore del Manchester United?

"Ero incredulo, non ci potevo credere". Ha raccontato così Pierluigi Gollini il giorno in cui ha scoperto dell'interesse su di lui del Manchester United. Un interesse che poi diventò una trattativa vera e propria, con i Red Devils che portarono a termine l'ennesimo "scippo" di un giovane talento ad una squadra italiana.

All'epoca Gollini era un promettente portiere del settore giovanile della Fiorentina ed il suo passaggio al Manchester United fece andare su tutte le furie Pantaleo Corvino, all'epoca direttore dell'area tecnica viola. Un trasferimento discusso, che permise al portiere oggi titolare della Roma di vivere e allenarsi con campioni di livello assoluto.

A Manchester Gollini restò circa 2 anni, senza mai esordire in prima squadra ma appunto lavorando a stretto contatto Evra, Rooney, Giggs e Paul Scholes. Il suo biennio inglese andò avanti con la seconda squadra dei Red Devils, con qualche apparizione in Youth League, ma come ammise lui stesso "fu un periodo fondamentale per la mia carriera". Ora Gollini a Old Trafford ci giocherà davvero e lo farà da protagonista, con la maglia della Roma sulle spalle dopo le ottime prestazioni da quando ha iniziato a sostituire l'infortunato Svilar.

#2258. Cesar Peixoto must manage Wolves’ creative machine carefully with star potential emphasised in Cardiff City win

Wolves continued their improved run of form on Saturday as they defeated Cardiff City 3-0 at Molineux. The triumph made it 10 points from the last 12 available for Wanderers, continuing their fine response to back-to-back losses in the first two games after the September-October international break.

Cesar Peixoto‘s side were two up within 15 minutes thanks to goals from Fer Lopez and Adam Armstrong, Ladislav Krejci made it three just before the hour mark to really secure the points, heading home from a Kieran Tripper corner.

Alongside assisting the third goal, right-back Trippier was a standout creative threat for Wolves with the joint-most chances made at three – tied with Bluebirds winger Chris Willock. The 36-year-old and captain on the day showed why he has a key role to play at Molineux through his technical ability and leadership.

Trippier was Wolves’ leading creator on Saturday with his three opportunities made. He hugged the right-hand side for the vast majority of the match and saw a lot of the ball, with his 74 touches more than any other player for the Old Gold.

He completed 35 passes, 11 of which were into the final third and 14 of which were line-breaking. He made two accurate crosses too, showing how he mixed up his work in possession with deliveries into the box and others into spaces occupied by Lopez, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Armstrong.

Trippier did his defensive duties too, with 12 defensive contributions the joint-most in the game. He made four tackles, five clearances and three interceptions, so it was a very well-rounded display from the veteran right-back.

Creatively, his display saw the theme of his performances continue. Trippier currently ranks in the top 4% of Championship right-backs for successful passes (52.53), accurate long balls (4.35), line-breaking passes (16.39), chances created (3.01) and chances created (3.01) per 90 (all stats via Fotmob).

From deep areas on the right-hand side, Trippier is a major creative outlet and a go-to player in possession. This paired with his vast experience and leadership from a storied career to date make him a crucial asset for Wolves.

There are few doubts over what Trippier can contribute at Wolves. His past at the very top of club and international football means he provides a level of pedigree few in the Championship can offer, and he sets an example on and off the pitch as a vocal leader.

He’s a standout creatively too, serving as a key asset in possession and from set-pieces. Such traits mean that, in an ideal world, Trippier could play every minute of every match.

However, at 36 and with injury issues arising over his last two years at Newcastle United and early on this term, Peixoto faces the challenge of managing his workload. Trippier can not be expected to play every minute of a Championship season, so they must be careful not to demand too much of the right-back to limit the risk of injury.

It will be a tough balance to strike, but it is key to getting the best out of him all season. Trippier needs to be rotated with Jackson Tchatchoua to keep him fit and at the top of his game.

#2257. Meret a SKY: “Non è un momento facile. Gruppo svuotato? Possiamo solo continuare a lavorare”

Alex Meret, portiere del Napoli, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni a Sky Sport, dopo la sconfitta contro la Juventus: “Gli infortuni e gli indisponibili ne abbiamo diversi, ma chi c’è deve fare bene e deve lottare, sacrificandosi per il Napoli. Potevamo fare di più, è stata una partita equilibrata, i dettagli hanno fatto la differenza, noi dobbiamo fare meglio sotto tutti gli aspetti, se abbiamo perso tanti punti un motivo c’è, dobbiamo risalire in classifica. Non è un momento facile, non stiamo trovando continuità, ma siamo tutti uniti e vogliosi di riprenderci, il gruppo unito e da domani lavoriamo per la prossima partita. Le motivazioni non le so, se le sapessi sarebbe più facile risolvere la situazione, siamo dispiaciuti, noi possiamo continuare a lavorare per fare meglio dalla prossima partita”.

#2256. Stato di forma: Bologna e Genoa sul podio! Il Como vola anche con la Champions

Qual è lo stato di forma delle venti partecipanti alla Serie A 2026/27? In questo focus vi proponiamo la classifica in base ai punti conquistati dai club del massimo campionato italiano nelle ultime cinque partite disputate. A comandare questa speciale graduatoria c'è la Lazio di Gattuso che in questo lasso di tempo ha conquistato solo vittorie. Al secondo posto con quattro successi e un pareggio ecco il Como di Fabregas: nonostante gli impegni in Champions, i lariani in campionato viaggiano con una media da primissimi posti. Poi sul gradino più basso del podio insieme all'Inter di Chivu un paio di sorprese: oltre ai nerazzurri, a conquistare dodici punti negli ultimi cinque turni il Bologna di Palladino e il Genoa di De Rossi.

In fondo a questa graduatoria tre squadre: un pareggio e quattro sconfitte per Sassuolo, Cagliari e Udinese, con Runjaic che dopo l'ultimo ko interno è stato esonerato per far spazio a Paolo Zanetti. Tra le big deludono il Napoli di Allegri e la Juventus di Spalletti: sette punti nelle ultime cinque gare. Peggio l'Atalanta di Maurizio Sarri che ieri ha incassato un 3-0 casalingo contro il Parma e non vince in campionato dallo scorso 12 ottobre. Il Milan di Amorim negli ultimi cinque turni ha conquistato gli stessi punti del Frosinone di Alvini, la Roma ai piedi del podio uno in più. Di seguito il dato.

Lazio 15 punti Como 13 Inter 12 Bologna 12 Genoa 12 Roma 11 Frosinone 10 Milan 10 Torino 9 Napoli 7 Juventus 7 Atalanta 5 Fiorentina 4 Parma 4 Monza 3 Lecce 3 Venezia 3 Cagliari 1 Udinese 1 Sassuolo 1

#2255. Paolo Zanetti è il nuovo allenatore dell'Udinese

Dopo l'esonero di Kosta Runjaic, l'Udinese ha ufficializzato l'arrivo del nuovo allenatore

Dopo l'esonero di Kosta Runjaic, l'Udinese ha ufficializzato l'arrivo del nuovo allenatore, Paolo Zanetti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Udinese Calcio è lieta di annunciare di aver affidato a Paolo Zanetti la guida tecnica della prima squadra. Ha firmato un contratto fino al 30 giugno 2027.Nato a Valdagno, in provincia di Vicenza, il 16 dicembre 1982, Zanetti vanta una carriera da calciatore, durante la quale ha vestito, tra le altre, le maglie di Torino e Atalanta, collezionando anche cinque presenze con la Nazionale Under 21. Appesi gli scarpini al chiodo, ha intrapreso immediatamente la carriera da allenatore, guidando la formazione Berretti della Reggiana a soli 33 anni. Il suo percorso nel calcio professionistico inizia nella stagione 2017/2018 alla guida del Südtirol, con cui ottiene risultati importanti che, dopo due stagioni a Bolzano, gli valgono la chiamata dell’Ascoli in Serie B. La stagione della consacrazione è la 2020/2021, quando conduce il Venezia alla promozione in Serie A, riportando i lagunari nella massima serie dopo 19 anni di assenza. Zanetti resta sulla panchina del Venezia anche nella stagione successiva, prima di trasferirsi all’Empoli, con cui conquista una tranquilla salvezza nell’annata 2022/2023. La sua ultima esperienza in Serie A è quella sulla panchina del Verona, squadra che conduce al quattordicesimo posto nella stagione 2024/2025 e con cui rimane fino al febbraio 2026.Ora per Paolo Zanetti si apre una nuova sfida: guidare l’Udinese e iniziare un nuovo capitolo della sua carriera in bianconero.Il nuovo allenatore dirigerà domani pomeriggio la prima seduta di allenamento. La conferenza stampa di presentazione si terrà mercoledì alle ore 15.00.A mister Zanetti e a tutto il suo gruppo di lavoro va il caloroso benvenuto da parte dell’intero club.Benvenuto a Udine, mister!

#2254. Kieran McKenna on West Ham’s three-man managerial shortlist as Nuno doubts grow

West Ham slipped to 8th in the Championship after defeat against West Brom on Saturday. WHUFC are currently in the play-off positions, but back-to-back losses to fellow promotion hopefuls have brought concerns.

Now, reporter Alan Nixon states that the Hammers have a three-man shortlist of potential targets if they decide to part ways with the under-fire Nuno Espirito Santo. Nixon says that Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker are all on the radar at the London Stadium.

All of the names mentioned are currently available, but it remains to be seen if the interest develops into anything concrete.

West Ham have some favourable fixtures coming up, with Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth all to play before the end of November. This run could be crucial for Nuno as pressure on his position grows.

Unlike Championship rivals Burnley, who have recently appointed Fabio Celestini, it appears West Ham are looking for experience in the division as they weigh up potential Nuno replacements.

It may be hard to persuade McKenna to return to the second tier, however, Parker and Edwards may be tempted by the opportunity.

Parker has gained promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. He operated with possession-based football and defensive organisation within his ranks. However, his time at each club ended on a sour note in the Premier League with relegation campaigns.

Edwards has also gained promotion from the division with Luton Town, whilst showing positive signs at the likes of Middlesbrough. He deploys his sides with a compact, high-energy system, putting an emphasis on pressing and attacking width.

McKenna meanwhile has only managed Ipswich Town, taking them from League One to the Premier League. He left the club earlier this year, but the Tractor Boys would still be owed a sizeable compensation fee.

Although Parker has multiple promotions on his CV, a move for the Englishman may be a risk. He might take West Ham out of the Championship, but his spells at other clubs has indicated that he may not be able to keep them in the Premier League if they return.

McKenna would be a very exciting appointment for West Ham, however it would be a surprise to see him drop to the Championship again. He is the most attractive target of the three, but the most unlikely.

Edwards, may be a more feasible appointment though. He’s proven his promotion pedigree in the Championship and takes pride two things WHUFC are currently lacking: defensive organisation and battling spirit.

Time will tell if Nuno can turn the tide, but the Hammers are seemingly prepared if they do opt for change.
