There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

INS:Andrey Santos ⇠ Chelsea, £48mYouri Tielemans ⇠ Aston Villa, £36mKarl Darlow ⇠ Leeds, FreeTynan Thompson ⇠ Tottenham, £4m

OUTS:Casemiro ⇢ Inter Miami, FreeRasmus Hojlund ⇢ Napoli, £38mJadon Sancho, FreeTyrell Malacia, Free

Forward JJ Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, is on the bench for Manchester United this evening. The 15-year-old has represented England at U15, U16 and U17 level. He won the inaugural Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season award for the 2025/26 campaign.

Starting XI: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire (captain), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J.Fletcher, T.Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

Dagens 11 utvalgte 🖤🤍Avspark er klokken 18.00 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/LuZrojJM4l

Bring on United! 🫡Watch Rosenborg v United LIVE on MUTV, with build-up starting at 16:00 BST 📲

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#2235. James Penrice's ‘turned a corner’ claim as Badredine Bouanani hails ‘crazy’ support

James Penrice reckons Rangers have “turned a corner” but insists there is still plenty more to come after they booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

The Ibrox side overcame Aberdeen 1-0 at Hampden, with Ryan Naderi grabbing the late winner to send Derek McInnes’ men back to the national stadium in December.

Penrice, who played in a more central midfield role before switching back to left-back, was delighted with the victory and hailed Naderi for delivering when it mattered. He said: “It is excellent. We stuck in there today and got our goal. It is a proper striker's goal for Ryan.

Penrice believes Rangers’ resilience was crucial as they kept pushing for the breakthrough despite the prospect of extra time looming. He added: “We were all pushing. We created a number of chances. You have seen this season the resilience to keep going until the final whistle. It has paid off for us.

“It is a proper striker's goal for Ryan, and he has been excellent. He has been our guy supplying the goals.

"We are buzzing to get there, getting into the final, and that is the main thing.”

James Penrice and Badredine Bouanani speak after victory for @RangersFC at Barclays Hampden 🔵 "We've kind of turned a corner... it's getting better" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/BBGIXZRbN2

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) October 31, 2026

Rangers have now gone 11 games unbeaten, and Penrice believes their previous meeting with Aberdeen proved to be a turning point. But he warned there remains significant room for improvement despite their impressive run.

He said: “Aberdeen last time was probably the shift. We have turned a corner, but it is still not completely there. We can do a lot more on the pitch and score a lot more goals, but it is getting better.”

Badredine Bouanani was named Man of the Match after an impressive display but admitted he was frustrated not to get on the scoresheet himself. He said: “I had a few chances. I need to work in training. I need to score one or two goals today, but it is okay.

"I am going to work in training next week and hope next game I will score.”

Bouanani also hailed the Rangers support after sampling the Hampden atmosphere. He said: “Crazy fans. At home at Ibrox, it is always special, and today was also crazy. Very happy about the win.

And the winger insists he is relishing life at Rangers. He added: “Since I have been here, I enjoy every game. With the teammates, they are really good. We can give everything for them.

"I enjoy every game, and especially today was crazy.”

#2234. Cardiff City vs West Ham predictions as Nuno Espirito Santo faces ‘real doubt’

Cardiff City come into the Wednesday night clash against West Ham off the back of a defeat to Wolves on Saturday afternoon. The Bluebirds were two down within 15 minutes through goals from Fer Lopez and Adam Armstrong, and a Ladislav Krejci header made it 3-0 just before the hour mark.

It ended a positive run of three unbeaten for City, who will be pleased to be back on home turf. Brian Barry-Murphy‘s side are yet to lose in their six Championship home games this season, and have won the last three at the Cardiff City Stadium against Charlton Athletic, Watford and Birmingham City.

As for West Ham, manager Nuno Espirito Santo is facing growing scrutiny after defeat to West Brom made it back-to-back Championship losses. The Hammers were beaten 3-1 by the Baggies as they failed to bounce back from a home loss against Southampton.

The dip in form leaves WHUFC in 8th – just inside the Championship play-offs, but four points off the top two. A third consecutive loss could leave Nuno in real peril with reports stating Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker are being eyed as potential replacement candidates.

“This game is not as clear-cut as some may think it will be. Cardiff City were in League One last year while West Ham were in the Premier League, but Wednesday night’s hosts definitely have what it takes to spring a surprise.

“The Bluebirds have come up and continued to play their way with possession-heavy football. It has worked well, especially on home turf, where they are unbeaten and on a three-game winning streak. The last triumph was against a high-flying Birmingham City side too, showing just how strong they can be.

“West Ham make the long trip over to Wales low on confidence and in dire need of a result. Cardiff’s style of play will mean WHUFC have to put in a real effort out of possession, and I can see this being a problem.

“The Bluebirds are not the tightest at the back, so the Hammers can find joy through Jarrod Bowen and co. But, on current form and as a stylistic match-up, I get the feeling that Cardiff City win this.

“That outcome would put Nuno’s future in real doubt.”

“Cardiff City have been a bit inconsistent so far this season since their promotion from League One. They are still getting to grips with life in the Championship.

“The Bluebirds have only three wins on the board from their first 13 fixtures this term to date. Their home form hasn’t been bad over recent times though.

“West Ham will need to be at their best to get something in South Wales. Pressure is mounting on WHUFC’s manager Nuno Espirito Santo.

“The Hammers have slipped down to 8th in the table and another loss on Wednesday could spell the end for their head coach. However, I think they will have too much quality for their upcoming opponents.”

#2233. Dave Challinor must follow Sheffield Wednesday trend Henrik Pedersen ignored

Dave Challinor was confirmed as Sheffield Wednesday's manager over the weekend, and was in attendance at Hillsborough to watch the Owls draw 1-1 late on with Blackpool.

There'll be certain things that the 51-year-old will want to change at his new club, who sit ninth in League One having taken two points from their last four games, but one thing he needs to keep is Ernie Weaver across his backline.

The Matt Hamshaw caretaker stint at Hillsborough won't be spoken about much around the terraces anytime soon, but one positive thing that the former Rotherham United boss did in the two games he took charge of was putting the 20-year-old back in the side.

Weaver's more than taken that chance, and what was once a season destined for a loan spell out of the Football League is now looking more than promising in League One — but only if Challinor keeps that faith in him.

Wednesday fans haven't left this past week's Hillsborough double-header with Cambridge United and Blackpool overly positive about the results, with both games ending 1-1.

However, they have had some positivity surrounding Weaver's performances in what have been his only league starts this season. The 20-year-old played just 48 minutes of league football so far this year under Henrik Pedersen, but completed both games under Hamshaw.

And that decision by the caretaker boss has proven to be a masterstroke. Weaver put in a defensive clinic against the U's last Tuesday, registering 20 defensive contributions, 11 headed clearances and six line-breaking passes.

His performance against Blackpool wasn't as perfect, but it was still a very solid one. The 20-year-old registered 10 defensive contributions and won all seven of his duels in the game, as the Owls almost held onto their lead, despite playing the better part of 50 minutes with ten men.

Weaver was starting to become a real fan favourite last season, coming through the academy and being one of the main stars of their EFL Cup wins over Bolton Wanderers and Leeds United.

In what was forecast to be a terrible campaign in the Championship as the Owls continued to protest the final months of the Dejphon Chansiri ownership, Weaver's emergence into the backline as a recently turned 19-year-old was set to be a rare bright spark.

Unfortunately, nothing was going Sheffield Wednesday's way last season, and in early October, the young centre-back went down with a foot injury, which ended up curtailing his campaign.

Relegation is never a good thing, but Owls fans were looking forward to being competitive ahead of this season with a good squad and newfound ambition under the Arise ownership.

They were also excited to see more of Weaver, who'd proven competent at Championship level already in his young career, becoming a staple of Wednesday's new-look side in the third tier.

Going into this season, there was still some speculation surrounding whether Henrik Pedersen would be the man for the job.

Despite having credit in the bank after taking on the thankless task of navigating last season at Hillsborough, some felt that the new era needed someone more capable in the dugout immediately.

Those groans of discontent grew louder as the season went on, and Pedersen's treatment of Weaver was one of the few avenues that Wednesday fans would go down when stating that he should be moved on.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

As mentioned, the 20-year-old only played 48 League One minutes under the former boss, none of which came in his final six league games in charge at Hillsborough. There was even talk of a loan move to National League side Forest Green Rovers in early October, with an EFL loan move impossible outside the transfer window.

Pedersen would opt for Gabriel Otegbayo as one of his reserve defenders, whose performances haven't endeared him to Wednesday fans just yet this season. That just increased the demand for Weaver to get minutes and increased the discourse that Pedersen was out of his depth.

Ultimately, it's a decision which has aged terribly for the Dane in the week following his dismissal. Weaver looks to be settling in perfectly at League One level, and the longer he performs well, the worse Pedersen looks.

Weaver has shown under Matt Hamshaw that he's good enough to be one of the spine members of this Sheffield Wednesday side, and new boss Dave Challinor must keep him at the heart of the Owls defence going forward.

Not only is Weaver a promising talent who can impact games at third-tier level and help Wednesday climb back into the promotion picture now, but having just turned 20 a couple of months ago, he has such a high ceiling.

How big a role do you see Ernie Weaver playing at Sheffield Wednesday under Dave Challinor? Let us know in the comments.

If the Owls play their cards right with the young defender, he could end up banking the club a sizeable fee in the future. As for now, though, he has genuine cult-hero potential, given his leadership, academy status and the fact he was born and raised in Sheffield.

All eyes will be on how Sheffield Wednesday line up under Challinor. Ensuring that Weaver is part of that first starting eleven will go a long way to earning some early praise amongst Owls fans.

#2232. Derek McInnes ‘by hook or by crook’ Rangers verdict after booking final place

Derek McInnes hailed Rangers’ “perseverance” after a late goal from Ryan Naderi beat Aberdeen to clinch a place in the Premier Sports Cup final at Barclays Hampden.

The Ibrox side struggled for the most part in a low-quality first half but came alive after the break and in the 83rd minute, after coming close on a series of occasions, Naderi converted a strike from James Penrice for a 1-0 win.

Rangers will face Hearts or Hibernian in the December 13 final, with the Edinburgh sides facing each other at the national stadium on Sunday.

McInnes said: “We arrived with the intention of getting to the cup final by hook or by crook and we done the job.

“So I am really pleased, delighted with the players in the main for their perseverance, for keeping going.

“I have been involved with lots of clubs, I have been involved at Rangers with a far more talented squad who have struggled to get through semi-finals.

“Semi-finals aren’t easy to get through, particularly when we played the way we did in the first half.

“We were ponderous. When we needed to be quicker when we needed to be calm in the final bit, we snatched and made poor decisions.

“To have 75 per cent possession and have 25 shots, it’s not good enough to only have five on target, that needs to be said.

“But that’s for another day, today is about getting through to the final.

“It is so important for this group of players to feel that, it is so important for the club and supporters to look forward to a cup final.

“We need to keep arriving at Hampden, we need to keep arriving at cup finals and get the job done to win trophies.

“But the better team won. I thought we looked the team more likely to score, a team who was chapping at the door for long periods and the goal took a bit longer to come.”

The Dons went into the game with five players missing due to injury or suspension, but boss Stephen Robinson praised they way they coped.

The Northern Irishman, who won the trophy with St Mirren last season, said: “Obviously disappointed with the result.

“They scored during our best spell in the game as well which is unfortunate.

“But considering the week we have had, it has been really tough with injuries and they showed great character and courage.

“I thought we were really well organised, I didn’t think Rangers looked like they were going to score but ultimately they are a very good team.

“They have players who can come on and win the game, they spend millions of pounds on those players and that was the difference between the sides today.”

#2231. All 24 Championship clubs ranked by their longest-serving current player

Football can be a ruthless industry at times, with the turnover of players at all levels meaning it is increasingly rare to see one man remain at a club for a considerable period of time.

There are exceptions up and down the English pyramid, though, with several players in the division having represented their current sides for the best part of a decade, while some have even gone well beyond that.

From players who arrived as established signings to academy products, Football League World has ranked all 24 Championship clubs by the longest-serving member of their squad.

Considering this, loan spells away have not been counted as breaking a player's service if they have remained contracted to their parent club, while an initial loan that led into a permanent move has been treated as one continuous spell.

Showing just how much Birmingham's squad has changed in recent years, Ethan Laird is the longest-serving member, despite only arriving in June 2023, signing a three-year deal after spending the previous season on loan at QPR.

Laird would go on to experience relegation to League One and the Blues' immediate promotion back to the Championship, making him one of a small group of players present since the very start of the Knighthead era.

A product of Charlton's academy, Miles Leaburn signed his first professional deal with the Addicks in July 2022, and wasted little time making an impression, scoring on his senior debut later that month.

Leaburn joined the academy from Chelsea in 2019, while his father, Carl, made over 300 appearances for the South London club.

When he moved from Stoke City in January 2022, Adam Davies became Paul Heckingbottom's first signing, with the shotstopper operating as a back-up throughout his time at Bramall Lane.

His longevity, though, has made him the longest-serving member of the squad at 34, with 32 appearances for the Blades since his switch.

Just one day separates the longest-serving players at Sheffield United and Lincoln City, with Ben House completing his move to the Imps from Eastleigh on 24 January 2022.

In his first full campaign at the club, House finished as top scorer and picked up the Players' Player of the Year award, while his current deal continues until 2028, after signing the new contract in October 2025 before Lincoln's promotion to the Championship.

After completing a deadline-day move from Swansea in August 2021, Connor Roberts is Burnley's longest-serving player, with Burnley relegated or promoted in each year since his arrival.

He didn't feel the brunt of one of these, though, with the Welshman spending the second half of the 2023/24 season on loan at Leeds before returning to the Clarets ahead of their second-tier return.

Jayson Molumby first arrived at The Hawthorns from Brighton in August 2021, joining on loan with a view to a permanent move.

That would go through a year later, with the midfielder now the Baggies' longest-serving player following the departure of Alex Mowatt, who arrived shortly before Molumby in July 2021.

In January 2025, Molumby put pen to paper on a new deal at the club, sealing his future in the Black Country until 2028.

Portsmouth defender Connor Ogilvie joined from Gillingham in the summer of 2021 and is now the longest-serving member of the squad after wholesale changes in recent years.

Ogilvie was part of the side that finally ended Pompey's lengthy stay in League One, when they won the league in 2023/24, before establishing himself at Championship level and signing a new deal in the summer of 2026.

For Stoke, Ben Wilmot is the longest-serving player, having made the switch on 24 June 2024, joining from Watford after spending the 2020/21 season as a regular starter during their promotion campaign.

In the subsequent years, there has been wholesale change at the Bet365 Stadium, while the centre-back has remained a permanent fixture who passed 150 Stoke appearances in 2025.

Josh Sheehan joined Bolton on a free transfer from Newport County on 7 June 2021, quickly after Wanderers sealed their promotion back to League One.

After George Johnston's departure in 2026, he is now the longest-serving member of Steven Schumacher's squad, and the Welshman has signed a deal until 2028 after being part of the Bolton squad that sealed their spot back in the Championship in the 2025/26 play-off final.

In January 2021, Cardiff made a move for Crew Alexandra defender Perry NG, who has been part of the furniture in South Wales ever since.

NG quickly established himself and became one of the most dependable players for the Bluebirds, winning the club's Player of the Year award in both the 2022/23 and 2023/24 seasons.

He also played 40 times as Cardiff were promoted back to the Championship in 2025/26, earning a fresh contract running to 2028 as a result.

#2230. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

#2229. Middlesbrough face Hayden Hackney 2.0 situation involving Aidan Morris

Middlesbrough have started the Championship season in remarkable fashion, sitting two points clear at the top of the table at the beginning of November.

Almost a year into his reign at the Riverside Stadium, Kim Hellberg's managerial stock is continuing to rise further, and so is the belief that the Reds could be ending their decade-long exile from the Premier League at the end of the campaign.

The Swede's high-pressing style continues to get the best out of those who were already at the Riverside Stadium prior to a remarkable summer transfer window.

Whilst the majority of everything good that Middlesbrough have done this season has run through Will Lankshear, last season saw another 'Young Lion' make plenty of headlines in the form of Hayden Hackney.

Hackney's progression from the Teesside outfit's academy ranks to becoming the Championship's Player of the Season in just four years was well-documented, subsequently allowing Middlesbrough to progress both on the field and off.

It's fair to say Hellberg has adapted well to the loss of the 24-year-old, although a similar dilemma may arise again with Aidan Morris.

The 2026/27 season is Morris' third with Middlesbrough, having been recruited at the beginning of Michael Carrick's final season in charge for $4m from MLS side Columbus Crew.

During a disappointing campaign overall for Boro, the American made a steady start to life in the Championship with 35 appearances - 33 of which were starts - contributing two assists whilst also posting solid underlying metrics which underpinned his influence as an all-action midfielder.

His performances then went up another level last term despite the Reds' eventual agony in the promotion race and then the play-offs, and whilst Hackney's initial £16.5m sale was viewed as a blow, although an expected one at that, Morris' influence has only grown stronger.

Playing every minute of the league season thus far, the 24-year-old has scored twice whilst averaging 95.3 touches, one key pass and 6.5 recoveries per match, with former EFL icon, Kevin Phillips, labelling him as one of the three best midfielders in the second tier as a result.

Morris' current role in Hellberg's system isn't just allowing the 14-time USMNT international to flourish individually, but it allows for his attack-minded teammates to create chances at will - ones which are also being put away compared to last term.

As such, it perhaps came as little surprise to some in the North East when transfer speculation involving the midfield ace came to a head in late October.

After Morris' starring performance in the 5-1 rout against Bolton Wanderers, Tom Bogert revealed that clubs abroad have begun to stand up and take notice of his consistency.

However, the key takeaway from a Middlesbrough perspective is that Morris hopes to lead the club back to the top-flight, which is very much a possibility at this moment in time.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

Middlesbrough chairman, Steve Gibson, has developed a tendency to back his managers to the hill, and that has certainly been the case in terms of transfer plans.

However, the addition of Morris two years ago was the start of what has proven to be a key facet of the club's recruitment strategy, with a handful of subsequent Stateside signings having a profound impact on Boro's promotion hopes.

Adilson Malanda has provided a goal threat whilst demonstrating his ability to become a high-level modern-day centre-back, whilst Sebastian Berhalter and Max Arfsten have also made strong first impressions since their summer arrivals from Vancouver Whitecaps and Columbus Crew respectively.

Middlesbrough could receive £24m in all for Hackney should certain requirements be met during his Everton spell, which will certainly come in useful.

The club also netted a further £20.3m this summer through a sell-on clause relating to Morgan Rogers' £117m move from Aston Villa to Chelsea, and Morris could be one of the next in line to land Boro a major windfall.

Middlesbrough fans, how much of a profit could the club make on Aidan Morris? Comment below!

He is under contract until June 2028 at present, and his dream of leading the club back to the Premier League would almost certainly have a positive knock-on effect on his market value if it came to fruition.

It remains to be seen what the future holds for the relevant parties, and although the club have successfully adapted to losing Hackney, such a dilemma may have to be considered sooner rather than later.

#2228. 9 players set to miss Charlton Athletic v Bolton Wanderers

A massive game between two sides just above the Championship's relegation zone takes place on Tuesday night, as Charlton Athletic welcome Bolton Wanderers to the Valley.

After their three home games in this block of fixtures between international breaks saw them lose to a 10-man Stoke City side, get battered by Middlesbrough and let a 2-1 lead slip inside the final ten minutes against Bristol City, Bolton will be happy to hit the road, with seven points out of their last three games away from the Toughsheet Stadium against difficult opposition.

This one's slightly less testing on paper, with the Addicks currently winless in 10 league outings and on the back of three consecutive defeats, but Nathan Jones' side will be keen to turn that around and pick up a morale-boosting win at the Valley.

We may only be 13 games into the new campaign, but you get the feeling that this matchup between the teams sitting on 14 points in 19th and 20th could be key in determining which of these sides, who are keen to establish themselves in this division, will do so.

These nine players, however, won't be fit to play a part.

Reece Burke hasn't played for Charlton yet this season, as his injury issues continue to haunt him.

The 30-year-old has played just 35 times in all competitions since the start of the 2024/25 campaign, 17 of which came in his debut term at the Valley last year under Nathan Jones, who brought him to Luton Town in 2021.

An innocuous injury saw him out of their EFL Cup matchup with Tottenham Hotspur in late August, and it's ruled him out since.

In that game, both Charlton centre-backs were withdrawn through injury. While Billy Koumetio has returned to action, Collins Sichenje won't be seen for the remainder of the campaign due to a knee injury.

The Kenyan international has played just 10 times for the Addicks since his move in the winter window last season from Serbian top-flight outfit FK Vojvodina.

Rob Apter is currently out with a knee injury, too, although it's unclear how long this setback will keep the 23-year-old sidelined.

The former Blackpool man hadn't featured much for the Addicks this season before the injury, playing just 11 minutes off the bench in their 4-0 loss against Stoke back in early September.

Bolton will still be without captain Eoin Toal after he missed their 3-2 defeat against Bristol City with an ankle injury.

Trotters boss Steven Schumacher did state that the injury had improved over the weekend, but the Northern Ireland international will be getting a scan to determine the severity of the issue over the coming days.

Gavin Bazunu played a big part in Bolton keeping a clean sheet and earning a point in their last away game against Southampton. However, like Toal, he also missed Bristol City through a thigh injury, and won't travel to the capital this Tuesday.

Jack Bonham was given the nod to return in goal after Bazunu had replaced him following his arrival from the Saints, and he'll likely be the main choice again in the Irishman's absence.

Ethan Erhahon also didn't make the loss against Bristol City with a thigh injury. The midfielder also won't be available for selection on Tuesday night.

AI has decided which sets of fanbases are the most annoying on social media connected to League One sides

The 25-year-old has had injury troubles in the past couple of years, missing 15 games in his final year at Lincoln City and then 16 games in his debut campaign at the Toughsheet last season. This is his first period out of the side this term.

The excitement surrounding a potential John McAtee revival in the Bolton squad in the first few weeks of the campaign quickly died down as the transfer window rolled on, and more attacking firepower was brought in.

The 27-year-old hasn't featured for the first team in nearly two months, and has spent time with the Under-21s recently. He's currently sidelined with a knee issue, though.

The same for McAtee can be said for Ryan Hardie, too. The Wrexham loanee reunited with ex-Plymouth Argyle boss Steven Schumacher at Bolton this summer, but he's yet to make any real impact.

Can Charlton Athletic finally return to winning ways on Tuesday night? Let us know in the comments.

The 29-year-old is yet to start a game for the Trotters during his loan stint, and missed Bristol City with a hamstring injury. The same issue will keep him out of the trip to Charlton.

Canadian international Jayden Nelson is also yet to hit the ground running in a Bolton shirt, following his arrival from Austin FC in the MLS over the summer. He's also waiting for his first start.

The 24-year-old has missed the last three with a hamstring injury, and that run will stretch to four this week.

#2227. Ryan Naderi jokes he'll ‘stick to the easy ones’ after firing Rangers to final

Ryan Naderi shared the glory after his winner against Aberdeen booked Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

The Light Blues had improved after the break at Barclays Hampden after a mostly lacklustre first half and after several periods of sustained pressure, the 23-year-old striker pounced inside the box to knock in a strike from James Penrice in the 83rd minute – scoring his eight goal of the season.

Naderi said: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team.

“I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.

“I mean it’s a semi-final. No matter who you play against, they’re going throw in everything.

“They’re going to try to defend with every man. Also a big compliment to them because they did well. They threw themselves into everything and made it difficult for us to score.

“But as I said, we kept going, pushing for that goal and as I said, I think it’s a deserved win.”

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance.

The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well.

“So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones!

“As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Rangers will face Hearts or Hibernian in the December 13 final, with the Edinburgh sides facing each other at the national stadium on Sunday.

Asked if he felt the confidence will be there to go and win the trophy, he said: “Yes, we will definitely come here to win that thing, not to lose it.

“We’ve come this far so we want be there standing with the trophy in our hands, of course.”

#2226. Everton's £35m Burnley dispute has a new Companies House twist

Burnley have had a turbulent start to the season on the pitch with the club already changing head coach.

Fabio Celestini has arrived in place of Nicky Hayen, with the team struggling for results in the Championship.

The Clarets went into the campaign hoping to contend for promotion back to the Premier League, but are now in the mix at the bottom end of the table instead.

But the Lancashire outfit haven’t fared much better off the pitch either, with issues now surrounding the owners ALK Capital.

Burnley’s parent company Velocity Capital (UK) Holdings were handed a strike-off notice by Companies House for failing to keep up-to-date accounts.

It was reported by Burnley Express that the company have yet to file any accounts since being formed in 2023, with ALK Capital assuring supporters that they are working with Companies House to resolve the matter.

Fabio Celestini will look to make his mark quickly with Burnley after he was named as Nicky Hayen's successor at Turf Moor.

The business is at risk of being dissolved if a resolution cannot be found, and it is particularly concerning that it’s not the first time that Velocity have been hit with this kind of warning, as they were also hit with a First Gazette notice in February 2025.

This has brought a lot of unwanted uncertainty to Turf Moor, and supporters will want guarantees that it won’t impact the club moving forward.

Velocity is the sports investment vehicle under ALK Capital, who purchased a majority stake in Burnley through a leverage buyout in December 2020, buying 84 per cent of the club initially.

The manner of the takeover put the new owners on the backfoot with supporters, and their 2022 relegation from the Premier League didn’t help matters.

The Clarets have become a yo-yo club in the seasons since, going up or coming down in each of the next four campaigns.

But these issues behind the scenes have really come at the worst time possible for ALK, because the Clarets now look at risk of being relegated for a second season in a row, leaving fans quite disappointed with the direction of the team on the pitch.

Everton were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules in 2021/22, the year that the Clarets were relegated to the Championship.

And the Lancashire outfit were able to successfully argue to the league’s independent commission that the breach of the rules cost the club financially, as they would not have been relegated had the Toffees followed the rules.

Are ALK Capital the right people to bring Burnley forward? Comment your opinion below

This led to a decision that the Merseyside outfit must pay £35 million to Burnley, which included £26 million in damages and a further £9 million in interest.

However, the Premier League side are currently appealing the decision, which could lead to the Clarets needing to repay the money in the future, if that appeal is successful.

Everton submitted a request to protect their £35 million as part of their appeal, which was not granted.

The Toffees will be keeping a close eye on the situation surrounding Velocity, because if they are unable to resolve the strike-off notice with Companies House then the business could be dissolved.

This leaves open the possibility that Everton are successful in their appeal against the £35 million penalty, but won’t be able to receive a repayment.

However, at this stage, there is no immediate reason to believe that the club’s money is at risk if their appeal is successful, with the appeal due to start at the end of this year.

#2225. Haissem Hassan on Celtic goal drought, Maloney guidance & one area for improvement

In football, end product is the defining trait of any winger. From Jimmy Johnstone to Jota, Celtic have a storied history of successful wide men, with Haissem Hassan the latest man eager to make his mark.

Hassan joined the club for an initial fee of £6 million from Real Oviedo this summer following an impressive World Cup campaign with Egypt that ended in a Round of 16 defeat to eventual finalists Argentina.

So far in Glasgow, though, Hassan has struggled to perform consistently, unable to fully replicate the international displays that brought his name to the attention of several European clubs.

If anything, the 24-year-old has shown his talent in bursts. He breezed past Celta Vigo's Marcos Alonso last Thursday, carrying Celtic 80 yards up the pitch and winning a corner.

An apex showing in the 7-1 shellacking of Hearts stands out too, but Hassan has yet to find the net for Celtic.

Indeed, two assists in 15 appearances across all competitions suggests a winger still searching for that crucial end product.

"Defensive-wise I need to improve. On the attacking side I need the numbers on goals and assists," Hassan said. "I should not be losing my head about it. I just need to focus on training.

"When I get the minutes, I need to try to produce and contribute to the team's performance. I will focus on doing this.

"In terms of defending, the team in Spain asked me a lot as well. The teams you play against are also good teams and they asked me to defend more."

Haissem Hassan in action for Celtic. (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Hassan's lack of goals isn't for a want of trying. He forced Dundee United goalkeeper Jack Walton into a fine save after coming off the bench during Wednesday evening's 2-2 draw and unleashing a rasping effort from range.

He also rattled the left post after cutting inside and leaving three Hearts players for dead a fortnight ago.

"I am really keen to score my first goal for Celtic and also add assists," Hassan continued. "The goal feels closer and closer.

"The other day I was close. The game before that I assisted goals so hopefully it will come soon."

Seven of Hassan's 15 Celtic appearances have come from the start.

Manager Martin O'Neill isn't short of wide options, with Jota, capable on both flanks, recently returning from an 18-month anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Camilo Duran, the club's current top scorer, can play on the right while Hyun-jun Yang and James Forrest remain viable picks.

Callum Osmand has also started featuring on the left-hand side. Hassan relishes the competition for places.

"The wingers in this team are at a really good level," he said. "When I go on the pitch, I have to give my best.

"But the competition is good for us all. If one player comes out and does really well, the rest of us know we have to do even more. It's been really good so far."

Assistant manager Shaun Maloney guides Celtic's wingers, having featured out wide during his own playing career.

"Shaun helps me a lot," Hassan explained. "He is close to the players and always tries to help the players. He had a good career as a winger.

"Whenever he comes to me and speaks to me, I always try to listen and take it into account. Having him as a reference point really helps me."

Hassan qualifies to play for Egypt through his parents, though he grew up on the outskirts of Paris and speaks fluent French and Spanish. The transition to life in Glasgow, he says, has been relatively straightforward, even if a slight language barrier exists.

"I am happy here. It's a nice city," he adds. "I live here with my family and they are happy here, too. It is cold but it is good! It's a big city that has it all so I'm happy here.

"It happens in Glasgow that I meet fans. It's good to feel the love of the fans. I try to stop as much as possible and take a photo with them.

"I like the culture. But I have been living in France and Spain where people have dinner quite late. Here it's very early so it's the only thing I need to get used to!"

Despite the cold weather, for Hassan, joining Celtic was a simple call: "I made the decision myself to come over here. It's a big club and I thought it would help me be a better player and improve my career.

"I didn't have to speak to anyone else for those reasons."

Although still transitioning to life at Celtic, Hassan played for Egypt during the recent international break, starting two crucial AFCON qualifiers against Angola and South Sudan.

A double-header against Malawi lies ahead later this month.

"It feels good to play for the national team," Hassan stated. "You represent your country and it's a great honour.

"There is a bunch of great players in the national team and I enjoy playing with them.

"The games against Malawi are really important. If we can win, it would take us top of the table and give us the opportunity to play at the next AFCON."

For now, though, Hassan's focus remains on getting off the mark at Celtic.

O'Neill's side travel to face Falkirk on Sunday afternoon before welcoming Besiktas to Glasgow in the Europa League on Thursday evening.

Pointless from their first three fixtures, Celtic realistically need a win against the Turks.

"We still have five games to go," Hassan asserted. "A win over Besiktas would give us confidence and hope.

"If we win the rest of the games or get as many points as possible, we definitely hope we can qualify for the next stage.

"This game is at home. We have the fans with us and hopefully we can get a good result and move forward.

"I don't think the Europa League has been a disappointment as such. We have a good team, good management but the results have cost us.

"We are struggling a bit now. But we can improve and we'll try to play in the best way possible."

#2224. British football's top 16 toughest fan firms named and ranked by AI

A lot has changed in British football over the years, from the money in the game to the way of playing.

Many will argue whether that is for better or worse, but it’s fair to say that most would acknowledge the overall fan experience is much better nowadays.

That’s not to say the atmosphere has improved, but football grounds are much safer places today, with many families packing out stadiums to watch their favourite teams.

Previously, that wasn’t the case, as hooliganism was a major problem in English football, with trouble occurring at most games up and down the country, whether that was outside the ground or even inside the stadium.

Whilst it hasn’t completely gone away, it’s certainly not at the same level, but it’s still something that the police put a lot of resources into trying to stop.

With that in mind, FLW asked AI to rank the top 16 toughest football clubs in Britain…

Who takes the top prize for having the noisiest home venue in England, Scotland and Wales?

Wolverhampton has a reputation as a tough town, and Molineux can be a hostile place for visiting fans, which extends to off the pitch as well.

There have been numerous firms associated with Wolves over the years, including the Subway Army, who got their name from the underpass that visiting fans used to walk through to get to the stadium, where they were often ambushed by home supporters.

It’s a similar story with Stoke, who have a rivalry off the pitch with Wolves, and there was trouble when the two clubs met earlier this season, which is proof that it does still go on.

Stoke’s main firm is the Naught Forty, and they were involved in plenty of violence on their own patch and on the road. The Potters fans could make their home ground a fortress when it’s full, and it is an intimidating place for supporters to go to.

The third Championship club on the list, Portsmouth is another team with a fierce reputation off the pitch, and their main firm is the 657 crew.

That comes from the first train that Pompey supporters used to get to London, and they would regularly be involved in trouble with clubs from the capital, along with local rivals Southampton and a host of other teams, whether it was at Fratton Park or at away games.

Forest are another club with a tough reputation, so many fans would expect to see them on this list, with the Forest Executive Crew seen as their main firm.

In their history, older Forest fans saw the two European Cup wins, whilst they’ve also dropped to League One. So, it has been a rollercoaster, and the Midlands club have been involved in a lot of trouble over the years.

Sheffield is a football-mad place, so it does unfortunately spill over, and the Blades Business Crew, associated with the red-and-white half of the city, are regarded as a tough firm.

Of course, their main rivals are Sheffield Wednesday, but the Blades have also had run-ins with Leeds, and they are another club that has caused trouble up and down the leagues.

It’s no surprise that Birmingham are on this list, with the Zulu Warriors a well-known hooligan group associated with the Second City club, and as well as causing chaos with local rivals like Aston Villa and Wolves, there have been violent incidents with a host of clubs in the country.

Even in today’s game, St. Andrew’s remains a ground that can provide a throwback atmosphere, and the walk from New Street to the stadium is still a difficult one to police.

If hooliganism was once described as the English disease, it’s fair to say it didn’t take long for it to reach Scotland, and Aberdeen Soccer Casuals quickly developed a reputation as a tough firm north of the border.

They may not have the support base of Celtic and Rangers, but the Dons would often be involved in incidents with Glasgow’s big two, as well as Hibernian.

The majority of the clubs higher up the list have a huge fan base, and Leeds certainly do, with the Leeds Service Crew unsurprisingly ranked high by AI when it comes to naming the toughest firms.

Elland Road is still an intimidating venue, and the Whites often travel in large numbers, which brings trouble across the country and on the continent. Leeds have many rivals off the pitch, including the likes of Man Utd, Chelsea and Millwall.

Glasgow is a divided city, so many would’ve expected both clubs to be on this list, and the issues between Celtic and Rangers stretch beyond the football side of things.

The Celtic Soccer Crew were involved in a lot of trouble in the past, and, more recently, ultra groups Green Brigade and Bhoys have continued to cause issues for police and rival supporters at Celtic Park and on their travels, both domestically and in Europe.

Next up are Celtic’s bitter rivals, and, as outlined above, the issues in Glasgow and the sectarianism that comes with the fixture means it remains arguably the most violent fixture in Britain nowadays.

Rangers have always had a reputation as a tough fan base, with the ICF their main firm from back in the 80s. They also have an ultra group now, with the Union Bears prominent on the Ibrox terraces.

#2223. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.
